question: How does oWALNUTS compare with nutpie 0.16.8 on the fixed-16 posteriordb models over the same 18 Linux seeds that fix the WP72 headline against CmdStan, on ESS per gradient and ESS per second, and on gates?

design.arm_run: nutpie 0.16.8 at defaults (bridgestan backend, target_accept 0.8, maxdepth 10, 4 chains, default init), 1,000 tune / 1,000 draws; v7's nutpie cell code (run_posteriordb.py nutpie_model / run_nutpie / metrics) unchanged
design.reused_not_rerun: oWALNUTS and CmdStan cells are NOT rerun: they are read unchanged from WP64 (seeds 560561-560563 at f097391c, 620601-620603 at c5c60122; posteriordb_bench_v7_linux_v1/artifacts/{v7,ext}/cells) and WP72 (seeds 720701-720712 at c5c60122; posteriordb_ratio_robustness_v1/artifacts/cells). The comparison is same-seed. All were run on lane 1 (cores 0-3) of the same box.
design.nutpie_all_18_rerun: nutpie runs on all 18 seeds here, including 560561-560563 where WP64 has nutpie cells; WP64's 48 fixed-16 nutpie cells are used only for a reported same-seed repeat check, not in any statistic
design.orchestration_change: one child process per (model, seed) instead of v7's one per (model, all seeds), so a nutpie panic (v7/WP64 lotka_volterra: 'Failed to constrain', poisoned mutex) cannot mark later seeds as crashed without running them
design.gates: v7's: rank R-hat <= 1.01, bulk and tail ESS >= 400 on the posteriordb reference columns, zero retained divergences, finite draws, no error; ArviZ 0.23.4
design.run_order: models in WP62's fixed-16 order; seeds ascending (560561-3, 620601-3, 720701-12); strictly sequential; no reruns
design.timeout: v7's 2,700 s per cell; each child is killed at 2,700 + 600 s and the cell recorded as timeout_or_crash
design.binaries: the 16 nutpie libraries copied from WP64's Linux build (posteriordb_bench_v7_linux_v1/models/nutpie, bridgestan.compile_model with STAN_THREADS=true from posteriordb 28f8d3d, as nutpie.compile_stan_model does); their TBB runtime copied byte-identically into the lane (LD_LIBRARY_PATH) instead of loading it from WP64's lane

platform.machine: AWS EC2 c7a.4xlarge (AMD EPYC 9R14), Ubuntu 24.04, lane 1: taskset -c 0-3, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, files under ~/lanes/nutpie_18seed_v1/
platform.wall_label_note: Linux, core-pinned to 4 dedicated cores (taskset -c 0-3) on a shared box with other pinned lanes active (shared L3 and memory bandwidth): walls are 'pinned, co-tenanted'. Pass counts and ESS per gradient are unaffected by co-tenancy.
platform.per_second_caveat: ESS per second compares walls taken at different times on the same lane (oWALNUTS/CmdStan in WP64 and WP72, nutpie here), each pinned, co-tenanted with whatever other lanes ran then. oWALNUTS wall excludes its start search (v7 rule); nutpie's wall includes its own initialisation; compilation excluded for both.
platform.software: lane venv on Python 3.12.3: nutpie 0.16.8, bridgestan 2.9.0, arviz 0.23.4, numpy 2.4.6, scipy 1.17.1, xarray 2026.9.0, posteriordb 0.2.0, pandas 3.1.0, cmdstanpy 1.3.0

analysis.statistic: WP72's (c): per model, the per-seed ratio (oWALNUTS / nutpie) on seeds where both cells are status ok, median across seeds, geomean over models; a model enters with at least ceil(5n/6) = 15 of 18 paired ok seeds

quantities.per_gradient: min_bulk_ess_per_gradient (min bulk ESS / gradients_total incl. warmup; nutpie: sum of n_steps)

analysis.also_reported: (c) oWALNUTS vs CmdStan per gradient (WP72's 0.826, recomputed) and per second; nutpie vs CmdStan per gradient and per second; gates per arm /288 and per model; non-ok cells; stuck chains (WP72 rule: a chain whose mean is more than 5 reference sd from the posteriordb reference mean on some gate parameter) for nutpie on every model, per seed on hmm_drive_0, beside oWALNUTS and CmdStan; nutpie same-seed repeat against WP64's 48 Linux nutpie cells

N1.text: per-gradient (c) oWALNUTS / nutpie lies in [1.0, 1.4] (coordinator's prediction, 'given WP58')

N1b.text: per-gradient (c) oWALNUTS / nutpie lies in [0.55, 0.95] (this study's own prediction; see expectation)

N2.text: per-second (c) oWALNUTS / nutpie lies in [1.2, 1.8] (from WP64's house17 ESS/s vs nutpie 1.454)

N3.text: nutpie passes fewer than oWALNUTS's 239 of 288 fixed-16 cells

predictions.expectation_stated_before_running: N1 and N1b cannot both hold. WP58 found nutpie AHEAD per gradient (1.70x oWALNUTS, from warmup spend and its mass matrix), and v7's all-22 per-gradient geomean oWALNUTS / nutpie was 0.645 (Windows) and 0.837 (Linux, WP64). We therefore expect N1 to fail low and N1b to hold. N1 is registered as the coordinator stated it; if it was meant as nutpie / oWALNUTS, it is equivalent to oWALNUTS / nutpie in [0.714, 1.0], which is reported beside it.

rules: Freeze PREREGISTRATION.md and protocol.json in a commit before the first cell. Sequential cells; failures, crashes and timeouts are results; no reruns, no tuning after results. A driver crash may be relaunched; only an interrupted cell without a completed artifact may be rerun from scratch with the same seed, recorded in AMENDMENTS.md. Raw draws are checksummed and not committed.
